clue.text: Aim low to use this weapon successfully

definitions.text: Aim low to use this weapon successfully

parts.words: Aim low to use this weapon successfully
parts.note: a naval weapon set to explode at a chosen depth beneath the surface, so the user literally aims low at a submarine

explanation.surface: Advice on marksmanship: keep your aim down if you want this weapon to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim low' sounds like a shooting tip, but the weapon is dropped from a ship to burst under water.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-submarine explosive dropped into the sea and set to detonate at a given depth.

clue.text: Few can fail to be eligible to run, in this state

definitions.text: Few can fail to be eligible to run, in this state

parts.words: Few can fail to be eligible to run, in this state
parts.note: a state where almost any citizen may stand for election, so few fail to qualify as candidates

explanation.surface: A remark about a country where hardly anyone is barred from running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests racing, but it means standing for office; 'state' is a nation and its system of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by the people, where ordinary citizens vote and may stand for office.

clue.text: Quiet noisemaker produces a lot of silly talk

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a rattle is a toy or device that makes noise

explanation.surface: A soft-sounding rattle somehow generates endless chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prattle is foolish, childish chatter, a stream of trivial speech.

clue.text: Top gear!

parts.note: gear in the sense of clothing worn on the top of the body, the head, rather than the highest gear of a car

explanation.surface: An exclamation of motoring delight at reaching the highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' reads as a car's highest gear (or the BBC motoring show), but it is clothing for the top of you.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental covering worn on the head, such as a feathered bonnet or turban.

clue.text: They turn to catch fish

parts.note: barbed curved bits of metal bent round on themselves, used by anglers to land a catch

explanation.surface: Something swivels round in order to snare fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests movement, but these simply bend round, curved so that a fish stays caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved barbed pieces of metal on a fishing line that snag and hold a fish.

clue.text: Part-song? Quite the opposite

parts.note: turn part-song round to song-part, a repeated section of a song such as a chorus

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece is a part-song and is told the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: A part-song is a choral piece for several voices; swap its two halves and you get a part of a song, the chorus that keeps recurring.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the recurring chorus of a song, one section repeated after each verse.

clue.text: These men don't hold change

indicators.note: these words hold the answer within them, spanning the end of one and start of the next

explanation.surface: These men refuse to keep hold of any loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' signals the letters held inside 'These men don't'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or alter a text, making changes to improve it.

clue.text: Suggests Ray's character is Greek

parts.note: a type of radiation ray is named after a letter of the Greek alphabet, a Greek character

explanation.surface: A claim that a man called Ray has a Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name and 'character' a personality, but it is radiation named by a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The third letter of the Greek alphabet, which gives its name to a kind of high-energy radiation.

clue.text: Get the wind up after hearing this!

definitions.text: Get the wind up after hearing this!

parts.words: Get the wind up after hearing this!
parts.note: to get the wind up is to become scared, but literally a broadcast alert says strong wind is coming

explanation.surface: Something you hear that would make anyone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the wind up' is British slang for becoming frightened; here the wind literally gets up after a storm alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast notice that very strong winds are on the way, as broadcast to shipping.

clue.text: Keep your distance if you show signs of this!

definitions.text: Keep your distance if you show signs of this!

parts.words: Keep your distance if you show signs of this!
parts.note: reads as a warning about infection, but someone standoffish is the one who keeps their distance

explanation.surface: A health warning telling anyone with symptoms to stay away from others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like quarantine advice; in fact keeping your distance is itself the symptom of reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness is a cool reserve, staying distant and detached from other people.

clue.text: Two forms of money taken off chocolate, for instance

parts.note: silver is coinage
paper is banknotes, paper money

explanation.surface: Some cash and notes are removed from a chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken off' looks like a removal of money, but it is the foil wrapping you peel off a chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Foil wrapping that is peeled from chocolate bars and similar sweets before eating.

clue.text: On the spot, might one say?

definitions.text: On the spot, might one say?

parts.words: On the spot, might one say?
parts.note: describes something placed or situated at a particular point, rather than someone put under pressure

explanation.surface: A question about whether one could call someone put on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the spot' usually means under pressure; here it is the literal sense of being situated in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Located means situated or placed at a particular site, on a given spot.

clue.text: If upset, boys can cause a disgraceful affair

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: lads are boys
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boys, if they are upset, can provoke a shameful incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If upset' rearranges LADS and CAN; 'cause' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a shocking event causing public outrage and disgrace.

clue.text: Blubbered, being killed by sailors

parts.note: blubbered here means having blubber, a fat-insulated sea creature hunted by seafarers

explanation.surface: Someone wept while being murdered by seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubbered' suggests weeping, but it means covered in blubber, the fat of a creature hunted by whaling crews.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest sea mammal, insulated by blubber and long hunted by seafarers.

clue.text: Describes all that's dear to us

definitions.text: Describes all that's dear to us

parts.words: Describes all that's dear to us
parts.note: dear in the sense of costly rather than beloved

explanation.surface: A sentimental line about everything we hold dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks affectionate, but it means high-priced.
explanation.definitionFit: Expensive means costly, high-priced; in British usage dear also means costly.

clue.text: Poet's son initially passes out, causing delays

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of passes
out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: A poet's son passes out at first, holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives P from 'passes'; 'out' rearranges that with POETS and SON; 'causing' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay something is to put it off to a later time, to defer it.

clue.text: Provides against a sickening possibility

parts.note: protects in advance against the chance of catching an illness, as a vaccination does

explanation.surface: Someone takes precautions against a horrible eventuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sickening' looks like 'disgusting', but it literally means making one sick, as an infection would.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect against disease, typically by vaccination, so that infection does not take hold.

clue.text: First, they opposed the Commonwealth-now venerate its head

definitions.text: First, they opposed the Commonwealth-now venerate its head

parts.words: First, they opposed the Commonwealth-now venerate its head
parts.note: supporters of the Crown fought Cromwell's Commonwealth, yet today honour the monarch who heads the modern Commonwealth

explanation.surface: A group once against the Commonwealth now worships its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commonwealth was Cromwell's republic after Charles I's execution; today's Commonwealth of Nations is headed by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of monarchy, notably the Cavaliers who fought for King Charles I.

clue.text: Need one for a dog to sell liquor — and many other things!

definitions.text: Need one for a dog to sell liquor — and many other things!

parts.words: Need one for a dog to sell liquor — and many other things!
parts.note: an official permit was required for keeping a dog or selling alcohol, among many other activities

explanation.surface: A list of things requiring official approval, from pets to pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain once required a permit for owning a dog, and still does for selling alcohol; the British spelling of the noun ends in -ence.
explanation.definitionFit: An official permit granting permission to do something otherwise forbidden.

clue.text: In the end, the judge will show the total raised

definitions.text: In the end, the judge will

parts.note: a sum is a total
up means raised

explanation.surface: Eventually a judge will reveal the full amount collected.
explanation.walkthrough: At the close of a trial the judge reviews the evidence for the jury; 'show' links the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's summary of the evidence to the jury is made at the close of the trial.

clue.text: Given rough handling, being treated like this?

definitions.text: Given rough handling, being treated like this?

parts.words: Given rough handling, being treated like this?
parts.note: rough handling that grazes a surface or rasps something clean

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether treatment like this counts as rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: Rough handling suggests violence, but a scraped surface is simply rubbed hard with something rough.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scraped is to have a surface rubbed or grazed with something rough.

clue.text: Apparently, members of religious groups are quite inhuman

definitions.text: Apparently, members of religious groups are quite inhuman

parts.words: Apparently, members of religious groups are quite inhuman
parts.note: split as ..., those within religious groups, yet the word names creatures that are not human

explanation.surface: Someone claims that cult members are utterly heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in two parts the word seems to mean those in religious groups; whole, it names creatures that are literally not human.
explanation.definitionFit: Small six-legged creatures such as beetles and flies, not human at all.

clue.text: Type of anchor lying on the bed

definitions.meaning: a ... anchor is a large spare anchor used in emergencies
a bedsheet lies on a bed

explanation.surface: An anchor of some kind has been left on the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a large emergency ship's anchor and a linen bed covering share this name.

clue.text: Troops don't start retreating, being left by wild beasts

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the word loses its opening letter, so it doesn't start

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers who won't advance are falling back, abandoned to wild animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes T from TROOPS, giving ROOPS; 'retreating' reverses it. 'Being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track, droppings or scent trail an animal leaves behind.

clue.text: A food is first of all put at risk -so nobody is partaking

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words is taken, first of all of them

explanation.surface: A dish is jeopardised, so no one is eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' takes the initial letters of 'put at risk so nobody is partaking'; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root vegetable, eaten roasted or boiled.

clue.text: Colour a wind instrument for the beginner

parts.note: green is a colour
a horn is a brass wind instrument

explanation.surface: Paint a brass instrument for a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a novice, someone inexperienced and naive.

clue.text: Knotty problem-so untie ropes!

indicators.note: untying loosens the word so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzling knot, so untie the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untie' rearranges ROPES; 'so' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, a difficult problem to solve.

clue.text: European attempt to get Jewish capital

definitions.text: European attempt to get Jewish capital

parts.words: European attempt to get Jewish capital
parts.note: medieval European Christians' campaigns to capture Jerusalem, the Jewish holy city, rather than seeking money

explanation.surface: A European venture to raise funds from Jewish sources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city, Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval military expeditions by European Christians to win the Holy Land and Jerusalem.
